Hello,
A blumat system uses a moisture-sensing ceramic carrot in the growing medium to control water flow. As the soil dries, it allows water to move through the tubing to the plant, so the key on the first use is setting up the water source, sensor, and placement correctly.

For a simple first setup:

Choose a water source. Use a raised reservoir for gravity watering, or a faucet, hose, or pump only with the appropriate Blumat pressure reducer.
Set the product correctly. If you have Blumat Classic, make sure the ceramic cone and tubing are primed and the reservoir is positioned correctly. If you have Tropf-Blumat, use the supplied starting setting for your pressure type.
Install the sensor. Place the ceramic tip firmly in the growing medium, about halfway between the pot center and wall, ideally halfway down the soil profile and no deeper than about 6 inches.
Connect the tubing. Connect the sensor to the supply tubing, then connect it to the dripper or distribution component, making sure the connections are fully seated.
Place the drippers around the root zone so water is distributed evenly.
Check the setup without opening the sensor. Make sure the tubing and drippers are connected correctly.
Test and adjust. Confirm water reaches each dripper, then make only small adjustments after the medium has had time to respond.
If you have not chosen between Blumat Classic and Tropf-Blumat yet, the most important first step is knowing which one you have, because the setup is different.
